target: Barusan ada yang mengetuk pintu, tapi tidak ada orang di luar.
english: Just now someone knocked on the door, but there was no one outside.
tip: Barusan = spoken 'just now'; in writing use baru saja. Barusan dia telepon. = He just called.

target: Kamu mendengar suara aneh itu barusan?
english: Did you hear that strange sound just now?
tip: Mendengar = hear (it reaches your ears); mendengarkan = listen (on purpose).

target: Malam sebelumnya dia tidur larut, jadi pagi itu dia bangun kesiangan.
english: The night before, he had gone to sleep late, so that morning he overslept.
tip: Sebelumnya after a time word = the ... before: malam sebelumnya = the night before.

target: Dia sempat ragu sebelumnya, tapi akhirnya dia menerima tawaran itu.
english: He was hesitant before, but in the end he accepted the offer.
tip: Sempat = at some point managed/happened to: sempat ragu = did hesitate for a while.

target: Cuci tangan dulu; sesudahnya baru kita makan bersama.
english: Wash your hands first; only after that do we eat together.
tip: Baru after a time link = only then: sesudahnya baru makan = only after that do we eat.

target: Sebelumnya saya minta maaf kalau suara saya kurang jelas.
english: First of all, I apologize if my voice is not clear enough.
tip: Sebelumnya can open politely: Sebelumnya, minta maaf... = First of all, apologies...

target: Ketika saya masih kuliah, saya sering begadang sebelum ujian.
english: When I was still in college, I often stayed up all night before exams.
tip: Ketika = when, common in writing; in everyday speech people usually say waktu: waktu saya kuliah.

target: Ketika pintu pesawat dibuka, para penumpang langsung berdiri.
english: When the plane door was opened, the passengers immediately stood up.
tip: Para + people-noun = plural group: para penumpang = the passengers.

target: Waktu saya kecil, ayah sering membacakan cerita sebelum tidur.
english: When I was small, Dad often read me stories before bed.
tip: Membacakan = read out for someone: membacakan cerita = read a story aloud (for them).

target: Dia menyapu halaman sambil menunggu cucian di mesin selesai.
english: She sweeps the yard while waiting for the laundry in the machine to finish.
tip: Sambil = while (same person doing both): menyapu sambil menunggu = sweep while waiting.

target: Kakak menonton drama Korea sambil melipat pakaian yang baru kering.
english: My older sister watches a Korean drama while folding the freshly dried clothes.
tip: Baru + adjective = freshly/just became: baru kering = just dried.

target: Pas saya keluar rumah, hujan turun deras sekali.
english: Right when I left the house, it started raining very hard.
tip: Pas = colloquial 'right when': pas saya keluar = right as I left. Written form: ketika/waktu.

target: Listrik mati pas filmnya sedang seru-serunya.
english: The power went out right when the movie was at its most exciting.
tip: Sedang + doubled adjective + -nya = at its peak: sedang seru-serunya = at its most exciting.

target: Antrean panjang itu akhirnya bergerak setelah loket kedua dibuka.
english: The long queue finally moved after the second counter was opened.
tip: Once antre (queue up) takes -an it's a full noun: antrean panjang itu – it takes an adjective, takes itu, and stands as the subject of the sentence.

target: Awalnya saya gugup, tapi akhirnya wawancaranya berjalan lancar.
english: At first I was nervous, but in the end the interview went smoothly.
tip: Awalnya ... akhirnya frames a story: awalnya susah, akhirnya terbiasa = hard at first, used to it in the end.

target: Awalnya dia menolak, akhirnya dia ikut juga ke acara itu.
english: At first he refused; in the end he came along to the event after all.
tip: Juga after the verb = after all/finally: ikut juga = ended up joining after all.

target: Awalnya rasanya aneh, tapi akhirnya saya malah suka makanan pedas.
english: At first it tasted strange, but in the end I actually came to like spicy food.
tip: Malah = contrary to expectation: saya malah suka = I actually ended up liking it.

target: Awalnya saya hanya mau melihat-lihat, akhirnya saya membeli dua pasang sepatu.
english: At first I only wanted to browse; in the end I bought two pairs of shoes.
tip: Doubling a verb makes it aimless and unhurried: melihat = look at, melihat-lihat = browse with no target. Hanya mau melihat-lihat = just looking, the shop answer.

target: Dulu saya tinggal di Medan sebelum pindah ke Bogor.
english: I used to live in Medan before moving to Bogor.
tip: Dulu at the start = used to: Dulu saya tinggal di Medan. = I used to live in Medan.

target: Dulu di sini sawah luas, sekarang sudah jadi perumahan besar.
english: There used to be wide rice fields here; now it has become a big housing estate.
tip: Dulu ... sekarang contrasts past and present: dulu sepi, sekarang ramai = used to be quiet, now busy.

target: Nenek dulu berjualan kue di pasar dekat stasiun.
english: Grandma used to sell cakes at the market near the station.
tip: Berjualan is selling as your trade, not one transaction: nenek dulu berjualan kue = grandma used to sell cakes for a living. To sell one specific thing, use menjual.

target: Tadi pagi saya bangun kesiangan, jadi saya berangkat tanpa sarapan.
english: This morning I woke up late, so I left without breakfast.
tip: Kesiangan = too late in the morning: bangun kesiangan = overslept.

target: Awalnya dia hanya membantu di dapur, lama-lama dia belajar memasak, akhirnya dia membuka warung sendiri.
english: At first she only helped in the kitchen; over time she learned to cook; in the end she opened her own food stall.
tip: Double a time word and it stretches into a process: lama = a long while, lama-lama = over time, bit by bit. Lama-lama dia belajar memasak = over time she learned to cook.

target: Ketika tamu datang, ibu masih memasak, jadi saya yang membuka pintu.
english: When the guests arrived, Mom was still cooking, so it was I who opened the door.
tip: Yang after the doer = the one who: saya yang membuka pintu = I'm the one who opened the door.

target: Awalnya kami salah naik bus, akhirnya kami turun di terminal dan naik ojek ke hotel.
english: At first we took the wrong bus; in the end we got off at the terminal and took a motorbike taxi to the hotel.
tip: Salah + verb = do wrongly: salah naik bus = take the wrong bus.

target: Malam ini saya ingin makan nasi goreng spesial pakai telur.
english: Tonight I want to eat special fried rice with an egg.
tip: Pakai adds toppings when ordering: pakai telur = with an egg.

target: Gado-gado itu sayuran rebus dengan bumbu kacang yang gurih.
english: Gado-gado is boiled vegetables with savory peanut sauce.
tip: Gurih is the savory richness of coconut milk, broth, and fried things – a core taste word English has no exact match for. Bumbu kacang yang gurih = savory peanut sauce.

target: Bakso di sini kuahnya bening dan baksonya kenyal.
english: The bakso here has clear broth and springy meatballs.
tip: Kenyal is the prized springy-bouncy bite: baksonya kenyal is a compliment. The opposite, lembek (mushy), is a failed bakso.

target: Ayam bakarnya manis karena diolesi kecap sebelum dibakar.
english: The grilled chicken is sweet because it is brushed with kecap before grilling.
tip: Kecap is soy sauce, not ketchup – kecap manis is the sweet, syrupy kind brushed on grilled chicken. English actually borrowed 'ketchup' from this Malay word.

target: Saya pesan sate ayam sepuluh tusuk, bumbu kacangnya dipisah, ya.
english: I'll have ten skewers of chicken satay, with the peanut sauce separate, please.
tip: Sate is counted in tusuk (skewers): sepuluh tusuk = ten skewers.
